note_on_method: Two of the five filter slugs have a lawful data driver in Austin. Outdoor does, because every published venue carries a stated outdoor count. Lights does, because the City marks eleven venues "Lighted during park hours", the first city in this directory where that filter clears the three-venue threshold on prose rather than on a GIS column. Indoor has no published venue yet, free has no driver because Austin never states a price, and public has none because access_type still has no controlled vocabulary.

slots.why_this_filter: Every verified pickleball court in Austin is outdoor, all sixty of them across twenty-one venues, so this page is the city's whole published inventory rather than a slice of it. Austin does run indoor pickleball inside its recreation centres, and the City lists it in a separate section of the same page; none of it has been verified yet, so none of it is listed here. Austin pickleball, as far as it can currently be vouched for, is a daylight-and-floodlight proposition, in a city where summer afternoons are not when anyone chooses to play.
slots.what_qualifies:
A venue appears here when the Austin Parks and Recreation Department states an outdoor court count for it on its pickleball locations page. Twenty-one qualify, from the single courts at Delta Pocket Park, Eastside Pocket Park, Mary Frances Baylor Clarksville Pocket Park and North Lake Creek up to the eight at the Austin Tennis and Pickleball Center.

Where the City gives two figures, as in "2 Multi-purpose Outdoor Courts with striping for 4 Pickleball Courts", the smaller is the count of physical slabs and the larger is the count of pickleball courts marked on them. The pickleball figure is what counts, so that venue is four. Publishing the slab count would understate Austin by nineteen courts; the pickleball count gives sixty across twenty-one venues, thirty-nine striped onto shared surfaces and twenty-one dedicated. Balcones District Park does not qualify: the City lists it with "striping for Pickleball" and no number, and the Census geocoder cannot resolve its address.

faqs.q: How many of these are dedicated pickleball courts?
faqs.a: Twenty-one of the sixty. The rest are lines painted onto multi-purpose slabs shared with other sports. Eight of the dedicated courts are at the Austin Tennis and Pickleball Center alone; the others are at Austin High Tennis Center, Pan American, Rosewood, South Austin, Delta Pocket Park, Eastside Pocket Park and Mary Frances Baylor Clarksville Pocket Park.

faqs.q: What are the courts made of?
faqs.a: Not verified at any of the twenty-one. Austin describes what a court is striped for rather than what it is surfaced with, so every venue on this list reads "not verified yet" on surface.

faqs.q: Do the courts have set hours?
faqs.a: Yes, and Austin publishes them for every venue, which few operators in this directory do. Fifteen run "Open Play: 7 Days a Week, 7 a.m. to 10 p.m." The exceptions matter: Pan American loses its courts to roller derby on Tuesday and Thursday evenings and weekend mornings from 9 a.m., Austin High follows the school calendar, Hancock closes midday in term time, and South Austin opens at 8 a.m. rather than 7.

faqs.q: Which venues are in Williamson County?
faqs.a: North Lake Creek and Springwoods Neighborhood Parks, both at the far northern and north-western edges of the city. They are inside the Austin city limits and outside Travis County, which is why they appear on this list and on the Austin city page but on no county page.

slots.why_this_filter: Austin is the first city in this directory where a lighting page could be built from what an operator wrote in prose. Eleven of its twenty-one venues carry the words "Lighted during park hours" on the City's pickleball page: more than half the city's venues, and 41 of its 60 courts. In central Texas that is not a detail. From June to September the sensible time to be on a court is after sunset, and this list is the difference between a plan and a guess. The City marks the lit venues individually rather than making a blanket statement about its parks, so each entry stands on its own.
slots.what_qualifies:
A venue appears here when its own entry on the City's pickleball page contains "Lighted during park hours". Eleven do. The other ten carry no lighting statement at all, and they are absent from this page because nobody has said either way, not because the City has said they are unlit. Note also what the statement does not say: "during park hours" ties the lights to the park's schedule rather than promising a fixed cut-off, and Austin publishes the hours separately per venue, so read the two together.

Austin is the first operator to state it venue by venue in prose at this scale, which is why this is the first /lights/ page in the directory built from sentences rather than from a database field.

faqs.q: How late can I actually play?
faqs.a: It depends on the venue, because the lighting is tied to park hours and Austin publishes those per venue. Most of the lit venues run to 10 p.m. seven days a week. South Austin Neighborhood Park runs 8 a.m. to 10 p.m.; the Austin Tennis and Pickleball Center closes at 10 p.m. on weekdays and 9 p.m. at weekends; Pan American runs to 10 p.m. on Monday, Wednesday and Friday but only to 7 p.m. on Tuesday and Thursday, when roller derby takes the courts.
Unknown. Ten Austin venues carry no lighting statement on the City's page. That reads as "not verified yet" rather than "No", because a silence is not a denial.

faqs.q: Which lit venue has the most courts?
faqs.a: The Austin Tennis and Pickleball Center at Walnut Creek Sports Park, with eight, though it is also the one venue in the city requiring a reservation. Dick Nichols District Park has five and is open play, which makes it the largest lit venue you can simply turn up to.

faqs.q: How many courts does that cover?
faqs.a: Forty-one of Austin's sixty verified courts, including the eight at the Austin Tennis and Pickleball Center, the five at Dick Nichols and the four each at Little Zilker, Pan American and Rosewood. The ten venues with no lighting statement hold the other nineteen courts between them.

sources.evidence: The City's pickleball locations page, carrying per venue a street address, a court count, opening hours, and at eleven venues the words "Lighted during park hours". Also "Reservations Required" at the Austin Tennis and Pickleball Center and the roller derby restriction at Pan American. Snapshot: data/sources/austin/pickleball.html

Every published address was matched and placed in the incorporated place "Austin city". 12017 Amherst Dr, the address the City gives for Balcones District Park, returned no match. Snapshot: data/sources/austin-county-census.json
